'''''A Cook's Tour''''' is a travel and food show that aired on [[Food Network]]. Host [[Anthony Bourdain]] visits various countries and cities worldwide where hosts treat him to local culture and cuisine. Two seasons of episodes were produced in 2000 and 2001 and first aired from January 2002 to 2003 in the United States on the Food Network. As of 2023, the series is formally available across multiple online platforms such as [[YouTube]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Bourdain's A Cook's Tour on YouTube |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z7EufSNr1RA&list=PLpz7cLJ1_TwSLBsCZiO1b_O4YnlHAJiB2 |publisher=GoTraveler |access-date=19 November 2024}}</ref> [[Tubi]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Bourdain's A Cook's Tour |url=https://tubitv.com/tv-shows/539135 |website=Tubi |publisher=GoTraveler |access-date=19 November 2024}}</ref> and [[Local Now]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Bourdain's A Cook's Tour |url=https://localnow.com/shows/anthony-bourdain-a-cooks-tour |website=LocalNow |publisher=GoTraveler |access-date=19 November 2024}}</ref> through distributor [[Questar Entertainment]] under the GoTraveler brand.

==Production==
NYU film program graduate Lydia Tenaglia,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854866/|title=Lydia Tenaglia|website=[[IMDb]]|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref> working at ''New York Times Television'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/company/co0009397|title=New York Times Television|website=[[IMDb]]|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref> picked up the book ''[[Kitchen Confidential (book)|Kitchen Confidential]]'', and, learning that Bourdain was proposing an ''[[Innocents Abroad]]''-style travel journal as a follow-up project, picked up the phone and made a cold call.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.producersguild.org/blogpost/923036/287989/LYDIA-TENAGLIA--When-It-Comes-To-Embracing-New-Frontiers-In-Nonfiction-TV-The-Producer-and-PGA-Member-Has-No-Reservations|title=Lydia Tenaglia - Interview|author=Chris Green|date=25 October 2017|website=[[Producers Guild of America]]|via=producersguild.org|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://explorepartsunknown.com/southern-italy/a-qa-with-zpzs-lydia-tenaglia-collins/|title=A Q&A with ZPZ's Lydia Tenaglia-Collins|date=22 November 2017|website=explorepartsunknown.com|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref>

The show was filmed with two Sony [[Sony DCR-TRV900|PD100]] [[DV (video format)|DV]] camcorders.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2019/08/parts-unknown-anthony-bourdain-executive-producers-lydia-tenaglia-chris-collins-filmmaker-toolkit-podcast-episode-88-1202167745/|title=How Anthony Bourdain found his on-screen voice and changed television|date=21 August 2019|first=Chris|last=O'Falt}}</ref>

==Reception==
In [[Variety (magazine)|Variety]], Phil Gallo says, "For once, [[Food Network]] is putting on display food you can’t do at home — and they show that acquiring the ingredients isn’t all pretty before the meal hits the dining room table."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2002/more/reviews/a-cook-s-tour-1200552021/|title=A Cook's Tour|first=Phil|last=Gallo|date=7 January 2002|website=variety.com|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref> Bourdain's account of his trip to Cambodia in Episodes 5 and 6 of Season 1 has been criticised by professor of French and Film Studies at [[Clemson University]] Joseph Mai as "filled with tawdry stereotypes" and largely ignoring [[Cambodian cuisine]]. Mai contrasts them to the later [[Anthony Bourdain: No Reservations|No Reservations]] to reflect on Bourdain's transformation in ethics and understanding towards [[Cambodia]] and [[History of Cambodia|its history]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Mai |first=Joseph |date=August 2018 |title=Humble pies |url=https://mekongreview.com/humble-pies/ |issue=12 |journal=[[Mekong Review]] |quote=Unfortunately, his account of his trip to Cambodia in 2000 is filled with tawdry stereotypes: abject poverty in the city, comparisons to the Stone Age in the countryside, dirty hovels for hotels, reminders to keep clean condoms, news stories from the ''Phnom Penh Post'' about acid attacks and child rape. ... Cambodian cuisine? Barely mentioned. |access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref>
